scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 7 (RT-TRM processor temperature, frequency and task-rate traces at ambient 25/30/35 C), with Tables 2 and 3 on page 8 giving platform and task parameters
scenario.description: RT-TRM (adaptive parameter assignment plus online idle-time scheduling) running on a real i.MX6 platform. The experiment records measured on-chip temperature, DVFS frequency and normalized task-rate versus time (0-900 s) at ambient temperatures of 25, 30 and 35 C, with Tmax = 60 C.
scenario.architecture: Freescale i.MX6 ARM Cortex-A9 uniprocessor with 3 DVFS levels (1 GHz/1.25 V, 0.8 GHz/1.15 V, 0.4 GHz/0.95 V) and an on-chip thermal sensor (0.4 C precision). It is modeled as a lumped single-node RC thermal circuit (R = 22 C/W, C = 0.0454 J/C) with no floorplan or block geometry.
scenario.workload: Six MiBench automotive periodic tasks (Angle-time conversion, Bit manipulation, Table lookup, Edge detection, FFT, PID) with the execution times and period ranges in Table 3 and the activity factors in Table 1
scenario.operating_point: Tmax = 60 C; ambient 25, 30 or 35 C; frequency 1 GHz, switching to 0.8 GHz at higher ambient. Reported task-rates are 91.5% (25 C), 82.6% (30 C) and 65.6% (35 C) of the maximum.

original_setup.solver: Analytical lumped single-node RC thermal circuit (R = 22 C/W, C = 0.0454 J/C, Eqs. 1-7, Table 2), run on a real Freescale i.MX6 ARM Cortex-A9 platform. Ambient temperature is estimated online from the on-chip sensor with Eq. 20. No spatial thermal solver is used. (PDF pages 2, 6, 8)
original_setup.optimizer: RT-TRM adaptive parameter assignment (APAF): linear programming (GNU LPsolver) over task periods for each DVFS level, starting from the highest level and lowering it until a feasible solution exists. It maximizes the weighted sum of task rates subject to the thermal condition C1 and the timing condition C2 with minimum idle time. Idle-time allocation uses an online slack-reclaiming scheduler (Algorithm 1). (PDF pages 5-8)
original_setup.controller: RT-TRM runtime adaptation on Linux with Resource Kernel. It estimates ambient temperature every 1 s, re-solves the parameter assignment when the estimate leaves a 1 C threshold band, uses EDF ordering, and inserts idle time through a kernel idle thread. (PDF pages 6-8)
original_setup.benchmark: Six MiBench automotive periodic tasks (Angle-time conversion, Bit manipulation, Table lookup, Edge detection, FFT, PID) with the execution times and period ranges in Table 3 and the activity factors in Table 1. Tmax = 60 C. The scenario is Fig. 7 at ambient 25/30/35 C, 0-900 s. The baselines are EDF-A, EDF-W and RT-MTC. (PDF pages 4, 8, 9)

thermal_observable.location: Single lumped processor temperature (i.MX6 on-chip thermal sensor, 0.4 C precision). No spatial location or block.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum over the 0-900 s time trace of the RT-TRM run in the Fig. 8c comparison experiment (text on PDF page 9). The ambient temperature for this run is not stated in the text, so this is not a per-ambient value for the Fig. 7 cases. Fig. 7 gives only graphical traces against the Tmax = 60 C limit, with no numeric peak.

physical_mismatches.reason: The source model is a lumped single-node RC circuit for one uniprocessor. It has no floorplan, block geometry, spatial heat spreading or per-block power map, so a spatial 2D or 3D chip thermal model cannot reproduce it.

The paper gives no 3D stack, interposer or chiplet structure. Package thermal resistance is only a lumped scalar (R = 22 C/W) taken from vendor data. Cooling and heat-sink details are not described beyond this.

The source result is a transient closed-loop experiment. It combines runtime ambient-temperature estimation, DVFS switching, task-period adaptation and idle-time insertion, with temperature-dependent leakage in the model. A steady-state or open-loop Studio run does not reproduce this controller.

The optimizer and controller (LP parameter assignment, EDF idle-time scheduler, RT-MTC feedback baseline) are real-time OS scheduling mechanisms. A chip thermal solver has no equivalent, so they are not replicated.

Power is given only as total-processor quantities (Pmax = 3860 mW, activity factors, average task powers in Fig. 2). No per-block power rows are published, and total power must not be split without a published rule.
No reliability or lifetime metric is evaluated. Only the Tmax = 60 C constraint and the percentage of time it is violated are used.

studio_assumptions: No pinned packet assets are supplied, so no Studio package or material assumptions are recorded. None are asserted as matching the paper.
Any Studio run would be a separate illustrative construction that is not paper-derived. Its coordinates and temperatures must not be compared numerically to the paper's 59.6 C.
missing_inputs: No pinned assets in the packet: no chiplet config, thermal config, code, parameter files or repository.
The linked URLs (lpsolve, Freescale AN4509, Freescale thermal white paper) are reference citations on PDF page 10. They are not paper artifacts and do not prove the experiment inputs exist.
No block names or x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m for the i.MX6 die or package.
No per-block power_rows. Only the total Pmax = 3860 mW and the per-task activity factors and average powers are published, with no published rule to split them across blocks.
No numeric Fig. 7 temperature, frequency or task-rate time series. Digitizing would carry uncertainty, and the figure is not machine-readable in the packet.
No numeric ambient temperature trace (Fig. 1) and no ambient condition for the 59.6 C maximum in Fig. 8c.
No die area, material stack, heat-sink or cooling parameters, and no boundary conditions beyond the lumped R and C.
No published 3D, interposer or chiplet structure, so no complete spatial experiment can be formed. The floorplan should be returned empty.
